title: Flask/Vue read-status filter
task_summary: Specify a user-facing All/Read/Unread filter implemented across the Vue client and Flask API while preserving CRUD behavior.

required_outcomes.outcome: The Books page presents visible All, Read, and Unread filter choices and visibly identifies the active choice.
required_outcomes.why_required: The requested user-facing capability needs understandable selectable states.

required_outcomes.outcome: All is the initial filter and requests the existing unfiltered `GET /books` behavior.
required_outcomes.why_required: The request preserves the current list as the default view.

required_outcomes.outcome: Read and Unread request server-filtered collections through the optional `read` query parameter on `GET /books`.
required_outcomes.why_required: The task explicitly crosses the frontend/backend boundary instead of filtering only an already downloaded collection.

required_outcomes.outcome: The Flask route interprets the supported read-filter values and returns only books with the requested boolean read state.
required_outcomes.why_required: The server owns the requested filtering behavior.

required_outcomes.outcome: Filtered and unfiltered responses retain the existing success object and `books` array shape.
required_outcomes.why_required: The request explicitly preserves the public JSON contract.

required_outcomes.outcome: The table reflects the selected filter and shows a clear empty result when no books match.
required_outcomes.why_required: Users need observable filtered and empty states.

required_outcomes.outcome: Refreshing the collection after add, update, or delete retains and reapplies the selected filter.
required_outcomes.why_required: The request explicitly protects filter state across existing mutations.

required_outcomes.outcome: Existing add, update, delete, and unfiltered-list behavior remains compatible.
required_outcomes.why_required: The new full-stack behavior must not break existing CRUD workflows.

compatibility_constraints: Omitting the read parameter returns all books as before.
The response object and book fields remain unchanged.
Existing CRUD requests and success behavior remain available.
acceptable_grouping: BOOKS-1 and BOOKS-2 may be one UI filter-state requirement.
BOOKS-3 and BOOKS-4 may be one end-to-end filter-contract requirement.
BOOKS-5 and BOOKS-8 may be one compatibility requirement.
BOOKS-6 and BOOKS-7 should remain clearly observable even when grouped.
supporting_details: The specification may choose reasonable encoded values for the boolean read query while keeping omission as All.
The active filter can remain component state; URL persistence is not required.
not_prescribed: Exact boolean query spelling beyond a documented supported contract
Tests or documentation work as product requirements
task_scope: Do not change Vue, Flask, tests, or current user documentation.
task_file_scope: Create one task file with a Draft execution plan.
Do not implement the Vue or Flask change.

required_evidence: Flask API tests verify omitted, read, and unread collection behavior and the preserved response shape.
Vue component tests verify visible filter choices, active selection, rendered results, empty state, and representative mutation refresh persistence.
A realistic frontend/backend or production-adapter crossing verifies that a selected UI filter produces the matching server request and rendered response.
testing_expectations.important_crossing: At least one test crosses the production client transport and Flask HTTP boundary for the filter flow.
avoid: Testing every add, update, and delete operation under every filter and collection state when representative cases prove refresh persistence.
Exact internal component state shape, axios call sequence, or incidental object-key assertions outside the public response contract.
Replacing the required layer crossing with separate mocked frontend and direct route-function tests.
